# @tiavision/sinter-mail

> Email bodies in a sinter app, without an iframe: `mail.parse(html, options)` turns an email's HTML into a sanitized tree (the browser's own tree construction, every element's CSS resolved), `mail.plain(text, options)` does the same for plain text, `mail.mime(bytes, options)` reads a whole message (parts, attachments, OpenPGP steps), and `<mail-body data-sn-with="{ body }">` renders the tree as part of the page. Pure helpers: an email in a `file:` resource is plain HTML at build time.

Setup: `sinter({ libraries: ['@tiavision/sinter-mail'] })`; `export * as mail from '@tiavision/sinter-mail'` in src/sinter.helpers.ts; `export type { Body, Element, Message, MimeOptions, Part } from '@tiavision/sinter-mail'` in src/sinter.types.ts. Lazy parser: also `lazy: ['@tiavision/sinter-mail']` (a let over mail.parse or mail.mime is undefined until it loads; mail.mime's reader is its own chunk, `@tiavision/sinter-mail/mime`, about 24 kB gzip with mail.mime; mail.plain, mail.text, mail.bytes, mail.imageType stay ordinary helpers). In an actions module with the package lazy, every `mail.*` call is a stub returning a Promise: await each one.

- `mail.parse(html, { images, proxy, cid, media, dataImages, legacyDisplay, encrypted, consent })`: `images` 'block' (default: remote images left out, their box kept) | 'allow' | 'proxy' (with `proxy: '/img?url={url}'`, `{url}` once); `cid` a map `{ 'id@host': url }` (url a blob:, raster data:, path or https: URL) or a template with `{cid}`; `media` 'wide' (800 px, default) | 'narrow' (375 px), the width `@media` rules are evaluated at; `dataImages` the largest data: image kept (characters, default 65536); `legacyDisplay: true` (a mime part's `legacyDisplay`) drops every `div.header-protection-legacy-display` of the body (RFC 9788); `encrypted: true` (a mime part's `protection.encrypted`) blocks remote images whatever `images` says, origins still listed; `consent: true` with it: the reader clicked "show images" for this message, `images` applies again (never a per-sender setting). Invalid options throw. Same source and options give the same frozen tree.
- `mail.plain(text, { flowed, delsp })`: paragraphs, autolinks, `>` quotes (class mail-quote), `-- ` signature (class mail-signature); `flowed` for format=flowed.
- `mail.mime(bytes, { prefer, decrypted, verdicts, open })`: bytes a Uint8Array (a string is read as UTF-8) of an .eml; returns a frozen JSON-shaped Message `{ type: 'message', headers, outer, sources, reply, confidential, hpOuter, parts, attachments, calendar, steps, summary, problems }`. `parts` in reading order, bodies never joined, each `{ id, contentType, protection }` plus by `type`: 'html' `{ html, legacyDisplay, inline: [{ contentId, attachment }] }` → `mail.parse(p.html, { cid, legacyDisplay: p.legacyDisplay, encrypted: p.protection.encrypted })`; 'text' `{ text, flowed, delsp }` → `mail.plain(p.text, { flowed: p.flowed, delsp: p.delsp })`; 'message' `{ message, ref }` (forwarded, inline; its own `summary`, never `from: 'matches'`); 'report' `{ text }`; 'encrypted' `{ ref, step, reason: 'pending' | 'failed' | 'not-root' | 'over-limit' }`. Ids are IMAP-like paths (`1`, `1.2`, `1.2.1`; in a payload `<step id>/1.2`), unique in a message: a nested message's multipart root shown whole is `<id>.1` (its problems name the message part `<id>`). `prefer` 'html' (default) | 'text' in multipart/alternative (a wholly armored text alternative wins regardless). `attachments`: `{ id, filename (safe), originalFilename (display only), contentType (declared, untrusted), disposition, kind: 'file' | 'related' | 'calendar' | 'message' | 'pgp-keys' | 'encrypted', contentId, size, ref, protection }`. `calendar`: `{ part, method, text, attachment }`, text for an iCalendar parser, never HTML. `headers`: `{ subject, from, sender, replyTo, to, cc (Address[]: { name, address (null when ambiguous), group?, suspicious? }), date (ISO 8601 in the sender's offset, -00:00 unknown zone, or null), messageId, inReplyTo, references, list, autocrypt, raw }`. `problems`: `{ code, part, blocking }`, one per part and code; blocking ones stop every step near them, except those about the app's results (`integrity`, a plaintext over the limit, a part opened past the step limit), which fail their step and stop nothing around it; never throws on malformed mail. Invalid options throw a TypeError (`decrypted`/`verdicts` plain objects, known statuses, 'ok' needs `plaintext` Uint8Array and boolean `integrity`); results or `open` ids matching no step are ignored (`stale-result`). Cached by input identity and results by key and identity: never change an input or a result in place. `await mail.forget()` (or `mail.mime.clear()`) drops every kept message and the plaintexts it holds (on lock or logout; with `lazy`, use `forget`: stubs allow calls, not properties). Not opened: message/partial, message/external-body, TNEF, uuencode; no S/MIME yet.
- `mail.bytes(bytes, ref, { decrypted })`: the decoded bytes a Ref names (a new `Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>`, Blob-ready; `decrypted` needed for refs inside a payload; TypeError outside its source). `mail.imageType(bytes)`: 'png' | 'jpeg' | 'gif' | 'webp' | 'avif' by magic number, or null, never SVG. Inline images: for each `Inline` of an html part, `mail.bytes(raw, attachment.ref, results)`, `mail.imageType`, `URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([bytes], { type: 'image/' + type }))` in an action, then `cid` is that map; only a recognized type becomes a URL (a blob URL has the page's origin). Save attachments as application/octet-stream under `filename`.
- OpenPGP steps: `mail.mime` never decrypts, verifies or holds keys. `steps`: `{ id, part, state: 'pending' | 'done' | 'failed', kind }` with 'decrypt' `{ ciphertext: Ref, armored }`, 'verify' `{ signed, signature: Ref, micalg }`, 'verify-cleartext' `{ block: Ref, charset }`; ids carry a SHA-256 digest of the bytes, so results bind to them. Action loop: `r = { decrypted: {...prior.decrypted}, verdicts: {...prior.verdicts}, open }`; repeat `msg = await mail.mime(raw, r)` while a step is pending; decrypt → `r.decrypted[s.id] = Decrypted { status: 'ok' | 'failed' | 'no-key' | 'locked' | 'unsupported', plaintext?, integrity? (a boolean, required with 'ok'; only true accepts the plaintext), signatures?: Verdict[] }` (openpgp.js: `readMessage`, `getEncryptionKeyIDs()` non-empty, `decrypt({ format: 'binary', config: { allowUnauthenticatedMessages: false } })`; `integrity: true` only then); verify → `r.verdicts[s.id] = Verdict[] { status: 'good' | 'bad' | 'no-key' | 'expired' | 'revoked' | 'unsupported', fingerprint?, created?, signer? }` where `signer` lists only addresses the app trusts as the key's; `data-sn-then="results = $result"` stores the returned results in state. Only the root is decrypted on its own; other encrypted structures are 'encrypted' parts `reason: 'not-root'`, whose `step` id put in `open` (the reader's choice) makes the step: shown in place with `protection.opened`, `summary.encrypted` 'some', no protected headers. A signature outside a ciphertext (sign over encrypt, a signed multipart around an opened part) gets its verify step, but its verdict labels nothing in the plaintext and binds no From: decrypted parts carry the ciphertext's own `signatures`, or `signed: null`.
- Protection and summary: each part and attachment `protection: { encrypted, opened?, signed: status | 'pending' | null, step?, signer? }`. `summary: { encrypted: 'all' | 'some' | 'none', signed: 'all' | 'some' | 'none', from: 'matches' | 'differs' | 'unknown' | null }`, over every part and attachment, nested messages' included: a message-level badge only for 'all' (signed 'all' = one good root signature whose signer includes the shown From, and every part and attachment good with that From); per-part marks otherwise; warn on from 'differs' or 'unknown'; show opened parts apart; the badge is on the body, `sources` 'outer' fields are unsigned. Protected headers (RFC 9788 `hp`, or `protected-headers="v1"`) replace `headers` once decrypted (signed-only: with a good verdict); the protected From only with a good signature binding it. Replies: to `reply` (in a decrypted payload: the protected Reply-To or From; without protected headers, the outer From only when a signature inside binds it, else empty: never an unsigned outer Reply-To); quote decrypted content only when `from` is 'matches'; in an unencrypted reply use each `confidential` header's `HP-Outer` value from `hpOuter` (`[name, value]`, name lowercase; under `protected-headers="v1"` the `outer` value) or leave it out. Decrypted HTML: `encrypted: true` in mail.parse, `consent: true` after the reader's click.
- `mail.text(node)`: the text, for previews. `mail.links(body)`: every link with its text.
- `<mail-body>` leaves out what the email hides at the parsed width (`display: none`, and all inside it): its images never load. Parse again with the other `media` when the reader's width crosses a breakpoint: `<mail-width data-sn-on-media="media = $event.detail">` beside the `<mail-body>` emits `'wide'`/`'narrow'` (640 px, prop `breakpoint`) when first laid out and at each crossing; state `{ media: /** @type {'wide' | 'narrow' | null} */ (null) }` and `media ? mail.parse(html, { media }) : null`: parsed once, for the right width (starting at 'wide' parses twice on a phone and requests the desktop images).
- `<mail-warm></mail-warm>` (opt-in) on a page that parses emails in the browser: it runs `mail.parse` and the builder on sample emails in idle time, so the first real email is parsed at a later one's speed (the browser compiles and optimises the parser first; a first email is otherwise three to four times as slow). It renders an empty hidden element; about 4.5 kB gzip.
- `body.light`: the email sets colours of its own and does not say they work on a dark page; `<mail-body>` then puts `mail-light` on its root. `import '@tiavision/sinter-mail/mail.css'` (optional): the browser defaults emails count on back under `.mail` for apps with a CSS reset (tables and images as drawn, `content-box`, block margins; images at the email's own size, no `max-width` cap), `.mail-light` a light canvas, `.mail-scroll` a box that scrolls a wide email sideways.
- Quoted history and signatures: `part: 'quote'`/`'signature'` (classes mail-quote, mail-signature) from Gmail (`gmail_quote`, `gmail_signature`), Apple Mail and Thunderbird (`blockquote type="cite"`, `moz-cite-prefix`, `moz-signature`), Outlook (from `#appendonsend`/`#divRplyFwdMsg`/its header block to the end of the parent, wrapped in one div; `#Signature`), new Outlook, Yahoo, Proton; `body.quotes` when there is history. `mail.unquoted(body)`: a copy without it (the body itself when nothing is quoted or nothing would be left).
- `body.images.origins`: the origins of the remote images, for a "show images from …" control. A 1 × 1 (or smaller) image, a tracking pixel, is left out of the tree and of `origins`.
- `body.schemes`: `['light', 'dark']` and the like when the email declares its colour schemes (`color-scheme` meta or property, `supported-color-schemes`); `dark` also when it has `prefers-color-scheme: dark` rules, whose colours are written `light-dark(<light>, <dark>)` and follow the scheme the body is shown in. Absent: written for a white page (keep it light on a dark page: `color-scheme: light` around it).
- `<mail-body>` slots: `link` (`$slot.node`, its children through `<slot></slot>`) and `image` (`$slot.node.attrs.src` absent when blocked).
- `mail.progressive(tree)`: deprecated, gives the tree back as it is; `<mail-body>` renders a long body whole, quickly, through its script builder.

Styles: the email's own win over the page's (inline); the page fills in what the email does not set (fonts, link colours). Kept: colours, fonts, text, box, borders, tables, display, float. Never: position, url(), web fonts, :hover, negative margins.

CSP: rendered in the browser, nothing beyond `script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'`. Folded at build time (file: emails): `style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'`.

MIME: bounded (32 levels, 1,000 parts, 8 nested messages, 16 steps, 256 MiB per call, payload 64 MiB), no throw on malformed mail, encoded words decoded only after tokenizing, controls removed from decoded values, filenames made safe, a blocking problem near crypto means no step and no badge.

Security: nothing runs (no script, handler, javascript: link, SVG, form, iframe), nothing loads without the app (images blocked or through its proxy, no CSS url()), nothing leaves the email's box, no class or stylesheet reaches the page, ids only for in-email links (prefixed mail-), `role` only as `presentation`/`none` on a layout table.

Guide: docs/mail.md. Design: docs/proposals/sinter-mail.md, docs/proposals/sinter-mail-mime.md.
